 At Amaravati

sentences.text:
Two Thousand And Twenty Four
 Present
 The Honourable Sri Justice V Srinivas
 Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal
 No: 2194/2017
Between:
Ap State Road Transport Corporation ...Appellant

And
Pedala Siva Kotaiah Kotaiah 2 Ors and ...Respondent(S)
Others
Counsel for the Appellant:
 P Durga Prasad Sc For Apsrtc
Counsel for the Respondent(S):
 Siva Prasad Katakamsetty
The Court made the following:
Judgment:

This appeal is directed against the order of the Chairman, Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- Judge, Family Court at Guntur (hereinafter called as 'the Tribunal') in M.V.O.P.No.505 of 2010 dated 28.06.2011.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- Judge, Family Court at Guntur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The appellant is the hirer/APSRTC of Bus bearing No.AP 07 Y 8702 (hereinafter referred to as "crime bus").
The respondent No.1 is the claimant, respondent Nos.2 and 3 are the owner and insurer of the said crime bus respectively.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter referred to as they arrayed before the tribunal.

4. The case of the claimant, in the petition before the Tribunal is that:
i).

On 14.02.2010 at about 11.00 a.m., while the claimant proceeding on motorcycle Ap State Road Transport Corporation vs Pedala Siva Kotaiah Kotaiah 2 Ors on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169284676/
1 bearing No.AP 7 AS 5271 from Perecherla to Guntur, the crime bus driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed the motorcycle of the claimant,
resulted, he sustained severe injuries.

entities.text: Ap State Road Transport Corporation vs Pedala Siva Kotaiah Kotaiah 2 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
ii). He claimed compensation of Rs.3,00,000/-
against the owner, hirer and insurer of the crime bus.

5. The respondent No.1/APSRTC/hirer filed written statement denying the averments in the petition and pleaded that the owner and insurer of the bus alone liable to pay compensation to the claimant and thereby, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

6. The respondent Nos.2 and 3/owner and insurer filed written statement denying the averments in the petition and pleaded that the crime bus was taken on hire by the 1st respondent/APSRTC and RTC alone liable to pay compensation, thereby, prayed to dismiss the petition against these respondents.
7.

The Tribunal settled the following issues for enquiry basing on the material:
"1.Whether the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bus bearing Regn. No.AP 07 Y 8702?
2.Whether the petitioner is entitled to the compensation, if so, from whom? and 3.To what relief?"
8. During enquiry, on behalf of the claimants, PWs.1 and 2 were examined, Exs.A.1 to A.6 and X.1 were marked.
On behalf of the respondent No.1/hirer/APSRTC, R.W.1 was examined and Exs.B.1 to B.4 are exhibited.
On behalf of respondent No.3/insurer, none were examined, but Ex.B.5 policy was marked.

9. On the material, the Tribunal, having come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the negligent driving of the crime bus by its driver, held that the claimant is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,00,000/-, with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization against the respondent No.1 only, for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
The claim against respondent Nos.2 and 3 is dismissed.
10. It is against the said award; the present appeal was preferred by the appellant/APSRTC/hirer.
11. Heard Sri Solmon Raju, learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/APSRTC and Sri K.Siva Prasad, learned counsel for the claimant.
12. Now, the following points arise for determination:

sentences.text: 2 1. Whether the appellant/APSRTC is alone liable to pay compensation?
2. Whether the Tribunal erred in exonerating respondent Nos.2 and 3/owner and insurer from the liability to pay compensation? and 3.
To what relief ?
13. POINT Nos.1 & 2 :

It is not in dispute about the injuries sustained by the claimant in the incident,
involvement of crime bus and motorcycle of the claimant, rash and negligent driving of the crime bus, the crime vehicle was validly insured with the 3rd respondent company by the time of accident and the same was running on hired basis under the appellant/APSRTC.
It is also an undisputed fact that no appeal was preferred by the claimant, owner and insurer of the crime bus against the findings of the Tribunal.

14. The only contention raised by the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/APSRTC is that when the vehicle was validly insured with the 3rd respondent/insurer, as per Ex.B.1 agreement between hirer and owner coupled with Exs.B.2 to B.4, the liability to pay the compensation to the 3rd parties is only on the owner as well insurer of the said vehicle, thereby, the Tribunal grossly erred in fixing the liability against the appellant/APSRTC/hirer by exonerating the owner and insurer to pay the compensation to the claimant.
15.
To decide the liability to pay the compensation, no oral or documentary evidence was adduced before the tribunal by the insurer.

Even, as stated supra, the crime bus was validly insured with the appellant under Exs.B.3 to B.5.
16.

On the other hand, the hirer/APRSTC got examined its official as R.W.1 and got marked Exs.B.1 to B.4 Original Deed of Agreement, attested Insurance Policy, attested copy of New Insurance Policy and IMT 44 Endorsement respectively.

It is the categorical testimony of R.W.1 that as per the terms and conditions of the Ex.B.1 Agreement condition No.5(iv) the owner shall liable for all claims, as per condition No.5(ii) the owner shall keep his vehicle duly insured comprehensively and as per condition No.5(iii) it is mutually agreed that the corporation shall not be responsible for any damage or loss caused to the vehicle hired during the period of accidents etc.
Furthermore, as per Ex.B.4 IMT 44, respondent No.2/owner paid additional premium of Rs.138/- covering the liability of the hirer, which is not denied by the 3rd respondent.
It is also not in dispute that the driver of the crime bus is having valid and effective driving license by the time of incident.
Thereby, the hirer is not liable to pay any compensation to the claimant and the insurer of the crime bus is only liable to pay the said compensation.

As discussed supra, no contra material was produced before the Tribunal to disbelieve the testimony of R.W.1 and Ex.B.1 agreement.
17.

Now it is relevant to make note a pronouncement of Hon'ble Supreme Court in U.P. State Road Transport Corporation v. Rajenderi Devi1, wherein at paragraph No.30 and 31 held as follows:
Ap State Road Transport Corporation vs Pedala Siva Kotaiah Kotaiah 2 Ors on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169284676/
3 "30.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Ap State Road Transport Corporation vs Pedala Siva Kotaiah Kotaiah 2 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, for all practical purposes, for the relevant period, the Corporation had become the 1 2020 LawSuit (SC) 429 owner of the vehicle for the specific period.

If the Corporation had become the owner even for the specific period and the vehicle having been insured at the instance of original owner, it would be deemed that the vehicle was transferred along with the insurance policy in existence to the Corporation and thus the Insurance Company would not be able to escape its liability to pay the amount of compensation.
31. The liability to pay compensation is based on a statutory provision.
Compulsory insurance of the vehicle is meant for the benefit of the third parties.
The liability of the owner to have compulsory insurance is only in regard to third party and not to the property.
Once the vehicle is insured, the owner as well as any other person can use the vehicle with the consent of the owner.
Section 146 of the Act does not provide that any person who uses the vehicle independently, a separate insurance policy should be taken.
The purpose of compulsory insurance in the Act has been enacted with an object to advance social justice."

18. In view of the above settled legal position and facts of the case, as discussed supra, it is clear in vivid terms that the 3rd respondent/insurer cannot be exonerated from its liability to pay compensation, on the other hand, in view of testimony of R.W.1 coupled with Exs.B.1 to B.4, the appellant/APSRTC is exonerated from its liability to pay compensation.

Thereby, the conclusion arrived by the Tribunal that the appellant/APSRTC alone liable to pay the compensation to the claimant and claim against respondent Nos.2 and 3/owner and insurer is liable for dismissal, is nothing but contrary to the law settled by the Apex Court.
It is needless to say that the rest of the order of the Tribunal regarding quantum of compensation requires no interference.
Thus, these points are answered in favour of the appellant/APSRTC.

19. POINT No.3:
In view of the findings on point Nos.1 and 2, the order of the Tribunal is liable to be set aside only to the extent of liability to pay the compensation to the claimant by the 3rd respondent/insurer.
Thereby, the appeal preferred by the appellant/APSRTC is liable to be considered.

20. In the result, M.A.C.M.A. is allowed awarding the compensation to the claimant against the respondent Nos.2 and 3/owner and insurer only and consequently, the 3rd respondent/insurer shall deposit the entire compensation amount within two months from the date of this judgment before the Tribunal.
The claim against the appellant/APSRTC is dismissed.
The rest of the order of the Tribunal regarding quantum of compensation entitled by the claimant shall remain intact.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Interim orders granted earlier if any, stand vacated.
Miscellaneous petitions pending if any, stand closed.
